findings.title: MonoGame.Framework assembly reference (install folder or packages folder)

triggeredRules.title: Import of MonoGame.Content.Builder.targets (installer targets)
triggeredRules.explanation: The project imports MonoGame.Content.Builder.targets from the MonoGame installer folder (MonoGame\v3.0). The installer is gone and the file does not exist on a machine with only the .NET SDK, so the build stops with MSB4019 (imported project not found).
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator writes an SDK-style project that references the MonoGame.Content.Builder.Task package instead of importing the installer targets.

triggeredRules.title: Import of MonoGame.Common.props (installer props)
triggeredRules.explanation: The project imports MonoGame.Common.props from the MonoGame installer folder. The file sets MonoGameInstallDirectory for the old HintPath references. Without the installer the import fails with MSB4019.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator drops the import. The SDK-style project gets MonoGame from NuGet and needs no install folder.

triggeredRules.title: MonoGame.Framework assembly reference (install folder or packages folder)
triggeredRules.explanation: The project references MonoGame.Framework as an assembly with a HintPath into the installer folder or into a packages folder next to the solution. Neither exists on a clean machine, and the version is fixed by the path.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator replaces the reference with a PackageReference to MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL or MonoGame.Framework.WindowsDX at 3.8.6.1, chosen from the old platform.

triggeredRules.title: MonoGamePlatform build property
triggeredRules.explanation: The project sets MonoGamePlatform, which only the old MonoGame installer targets read. It also drives the OutputPath pattern bin\$(MonoGamePlatform)\... and the platform that Content.mgcb is built for.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator drops the property. The target platform comes from the package that the migrated project references, and Content.mgcb gets the matching /platform.

triggeredRules.title: .NET Framework 4.x target (TargetFrameworkVersion)
triggeredRules.explanation: The project targets .NET Framework 2.0 to 4.x. MonoGame 3.8.6.1 supports only modern .NET, and a .NET Framework project cannot reference the MonoGame 3.8 packages.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator writes TargetFramework net8.0 (DesktopGL) or net8.0-windows (WindowsDX).

triggeredRules.title: x86-only build (PlatformTarget x86)
triggeredRules.explanation: The project builds for x86 only, as the 3.x templates did. The 3.8 desktop packages run as x64 or AnyCPU, and an x86 build of a net8.0 game needs a 32-bit runtime that most machines do not have.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator drops PlatformTarget so the game builds for the default architecture.

triggeredRules.title: packages.config NuGet list
triggeredRules.explanation: The project lists its NuGet packages in packages.config. SDK-style projects use PackageReference items instead, and the MonoGame and SharpDX packages in the list are replaced by the 3.8.6.1 package.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator turns each package that is not MonoGame or SharpDX into a PackageReference with the same id and version. A package it cannot map is listed as manual work. It does not call the network.

triggeredRules.title: SharpDX assembly references
triggeredRules.explanation: The project references SharpDX assemblies directly. MonoGame.Framework.WindowsDX 3.8.6.1 depends on SharpDX 4.2.0, so a migrated project gets SharpDX from the package. The analyzer cannot tell whether your code uses SharpDX types itself.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator drops the references that the package brings in (monogame-upgrade task 11.1). If your code uses SharpDX directly, check that it builds against SharpDX 4.2.0.

triggeredRules.title: Prebuilt .xnb files
triggeredRules.explanation: The project folder contains prebuilt .xnb files. They were built for one MonoGame version and platform, and a different MonoGame version can refuse to load them. XNA Reborn cannot rebuild an .xnb without its source asset.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator copies the files unchanged and lists them as manual work (monogame-upgrade task 12.3). If the game fails to load them, rebuild them from the source assets.
